title: Dycom: no buy today. Research target (12m) $294.37 says cheap, but the blended 12-month target $231.80 (+4.9%) clears no hurdle; revisit at or under ~$206 or on the late-November Q3 FY27 print
call_reason: The published 12-month target $231.80 is only +4.9% above $221.05, below DY's 12.3% beta-adjusted required return (binding: below_beta_return, so the book buys 0 shares), and rubric conviction is low; the price is above its Entry below level of about $206.42.
one_liner: Kilian's driver build, with the middle trim to the Communications backlog path he chose on 2026-11-02 at 7:26 p.m. ET, values Dycom at a research target (12m) of $294.37 (+33%) on only 13.2x NTM EPS, and insiders bought in September, but the options market (12-month median $208.08, P(gain) 46%) weighs 67% of the published target and sees a carrier-capex slowdown after AT&T's 10-21 capex cut and MasTec's Communications slump. We do not buy today; we buy at or under about $206, or re-underwrite after the late-November Q3 FY27 print shows whether Communications backlog is still growing.

thesis.point: The driver build (approved set plus Kilian's middle backlog trim) gives a research target (12m) of $294.37, +33% from $221.05, on a multiple well below peers.
thesis.evidence: Horizon NTM P/E 13.2x (own 12.13x today vs 18.65x whole-company peer median of MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) weighted 0.7 ($288.63) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA weighted 0.3 ($307.76); the five independent forecasts, made before the trim, span $299.55-$315.37 (the trim takes -2.7% off the untrimmed $302.46). Build EPS FY27 ~18.3-18.5 vs Zacks 15.98 and StockAnalysis 17.06.

thesis.point: Demand is slowing, not breaking: Communications backlog is flat while carrier capex is trimmed, and BEAD and long-haul land mostly after the 12-month horizon.
thesis.evidence: DY NTM Communications backlog 5,376 (Q1 FY27) -> 5,362 (Q2 FY27), flat; the path now in the set (Kilian's middle trim, 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET) needs 5,420 in Q3 and 5,580 in Q4 (was 5,450 / 5,650), then +1.75% a quarter in FY28 and +1.5% in FY29. AT&T cut 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B a year from $23-24B but kept >60M fiber locations by 2030; Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B. MasTec Communications backlog fell 7.5% q/q (flat y/y) with customer deferrals. All 56 BEAD final proposals are approved; >270,000 route miles, ~58% buried, construction 'in earnest' in FY28.

thesis.point: Insiders bought near current levels and the company keeps beating its own guide, which supports the base case through the Q3 print.
thesis.evidence: Open-market purchases: CEO 850 shares at $296.76 (09-09), directors 700 at $286.92 (09-01) and 350 at $280.62 (09-23). Q3 FY27 guide adj. EPS $4.33-4.79; the build carries ~5.2, Street 4.33 (whisper 4.55, 80% range 4.24-4.88), after six straight EPS beats of the guide midpoint.

variant_view: Two consensus views bracket us. Sell-side analysts (11, Strong Buy, median $525, mean $520.91, range $375-625, as of 10-09) are stale, set mostly May-September before the 61% fall from $566.47, and get zero weight in the target. The options market's 12-month distribution is the other pole: median $208.08 (below spot), 15th-85th range $111.42-$312.30, P(gain) 46%, with 1-year implied volatility ~60%. Our research leg (median $268.97, P(gain) 63.5%) is more constructive because the build follows DY's beat record and puts BEAD, long-haul and data-center work into the multiple; the published blend (67% market, 33% research) lands at $231.80. So the variant view is real on value (research target (12m) $294.37 vs options median $208) but not strong enough to clear the hurdle at today's price: the market is pricing a carrier capex slowdown (AT&T's 10-21 cut, MasTec's deferrals) that our path reflects only in part even after the middle trim Kilian chose on the supervisor's recommendation (four of five forecasters and the supervisor had called the original approved path full). Events past the 12-month horizon cut both ways and are weighed through the multiple: FTTH programs mature around 2030-32 (p 0.45, about -$12/sh), BEAD and long-haul extend Communications past the FTTH peak (p 0.5, about +$10/sh), a data-center construction turn in CY2028-29 (p 0.25, about -$10/sh), and carrier consolidation pricing (p 0.3, about -$6/sh); keeping ~29% of DY's discount to peers (exit k=0.8) is how the visible FTTH end date is priced.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $294.37 = model engine on Kilian's quarterly driver set (Communications NTM backlog, conversion and margin; Building Systems share of US private data-center construction and margin), with the Communications backlog path set by his middle-trim decision: NTM P/E 13.2x ($288.63, weight 0.7) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA ($307.76, weight 0.3), net debt 2,479.7 at 2026-08-01 rolled with FCF less $70M a year of buybacks, less 204.3 of debt-like supplier finance, ~30.0M shares at the horizon, SBC costed once. Downside case (P10) $135.05, upside case (P90) $457.63; thesis break $165. No DCF leg. Published 12-month target $231.80 = blend of the options-market leg ($208.08, 67%) and research leg ($268.97, 33%); expected (mean) $263.41 (+19.2%), P(gain) 53.1%. Entry below = $231.80 / 1.123 (T-bill + beta premium, no dividend) = about $206.42. Judgment calls: (1) Communications backlog after AT&T's capex cut: DECIDED by Kilian (decision card 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET): middle trim (Q3 FY27 5,420, Q4 5,580, +1.75%/qtr FY28, +1.5%/qtr FY29; FY28 year-end 5,981.1, FY29 6,348.1), now in the set: $294.37 (-2.7% vs the approved path's $302.46; the agent_3 path would give $288.87). Still open with Kilian, valued on the pre-trim $302.46 base: (2) Supplier finance ($367.4M): debt-like part 204.3 on the payable-days test (recommended, in the set); none $309.27 (+2.3%); all 367.4 $297.03 (-1.8%). (3) DY's own trailing EV/EBITDA: pro-forma 9.44x (pre-close add ~69) -> exit 10.2x (recommended, in the set); as-filed 10.15x -> exit 10.8x $309.41. (4) Agent_4 variant: no (recommended; its backlog part overlaps the middle trim now taken); backlog part only $298.76; margin part only (-50bp from Q3 FY27) $290.25; both $286.73 (-5.2%). None of these changes the no-buy call: even the untrimmed build ($302.46) left the published target below the hurdle at $221.05.

risks.risk: Carrier fiber programs slow or are re-sourced (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of revenue)
risks.signpost: Communications NTM backlog flat or down again in Q3 FY27 (below 5,362) or book-to-bill under 1; Verizon guiding 2027 capex below $16B

risks.risk: Contractor pricing and margin pressure as at MasTec (Communications margin 6.7%, -460bp) after carrier consolidation (AT&T-Lumen, Verizon-Frontier) and 90-day payment terms
risks.signpost: DY Communications margin below the 12.84% FY27 path; agent_4's -50bp variant alone was worth -4% ($290.25 on the pre-trim $302.46 base)

risks.risk: Data-center construction cycle turns (Building Systems at a 20% margin on a share of Census put-in-place)
risks.signpost: Census data-center line falling for two or more months; hyperscaler 2027 capex guides flat or down; Building Systems margin back toward mid-teens

risks.risk: Working-capital and balance-sheet quality: $367.4M supplier finance (204.3 treated as debt-like), receivables up ~34% in six months, Lumen 13.4% of receivables
risks.signpost: Supplier finance balance rising further or operating cash flow lagging EBITDA in the Q3 10-Q

trade.position: none: 0 sh ($0 of the $23,621 book; allocation binding below_beta_return)
trade.entry: No buy at $221.05. A buy needs the price at or under Entry below (about $206.42 on today's $231.80 target; it moves with the target after each re-run). If it qualifies, use the supervisor's plan: two tranches, half at entry and half after the Q3 FY2027 print once FY28 Communications commentary is out, within the supervisor's 4% cap (~$945).
trade.exit_or_add: Re-run the name after the Q3 FY27 print. Start a position only at or under Entry below with Communications backlog at or above ~5,420 (the trimmed path) and an intact FY28 Communications outlook; walk away if backlog falls below 5,362, a top carrier cuts a fiber program, or the price breaks the $165 thesis-break level. Once held: stop $156.09 (2 x 1-month implied move), take-profit $333.48 (75th percentile).

what_changes_our_mind: Price at or under the Entry below level (about $206, recomputed with the target after each run) with no new carrier cut: the 12-month target then clears the 12.3% beta-adjusted hurdle and the book buys.

The late-November Q3 FY27 print: Communications NTM backlog at or above 5,420 with book-to-bill above 1 and FY28 wireless recapture and BEAD timing reaffirmed would lift the research leg and conviction (the untrimmed path was worth $302.46); backlog below 5,362 or a cut in AT&T or Verizon work would push us toward the agent_3 path ($288.87) or lower and away from the name.

Communications backlog behavior after AT&T's 10-21 capex cut, read across Verizon's first 2027 guide (late January) and DY's FY28 outlook (early March): slower-but-growing keeps the research target (12m) near $294; a decline like MasTec's -7.5% q/q puts the downside case ($135.05) in play.
